title: The First $10,000 Is the Hardest: 20 Ways to Get There
description:
The first $10,000 is the hardest money you'll ever save. Here are 20 practical ways to get there, the math behind each one, and a simple 12 month plan you can start this week.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:31 How we got the numbers
2:01 Angle 1: The numbers
4:27 1. Name the goal
5:07 2. A separate account
5:45 3. Automate it on payday
6:25 4. Save every windfall
7:03 5. Track it every week
7:41 6. Cancel what you don't use
8:20 7. Negotiate your bills
9:02 8. Cut the delivery markup
9:37 9. Skip the car payment
10:14 10. Rethink housing
10:45 11. Sell what you don't use
11:20 12. Use a thirty day rule
12:12 13. Ask for a raise
12:48 14. Take the extra hours
13:20 15. Sell a skill
13:59 16. Consider switching jobs
14:31 17. Use rewards the right way
15:14 18. Stop paying fees
15:51 19. Earn interest on it
16:28 20. Save your raises
17:06 Three ways people get there
20:14 What to do once you have $10,000
21:53 Five traps that drain your savings
23:09 Angle 2: The psychology
25:13 Angle 3: The playbook
27:11 Questions people ask
29:18 Recap: 20 ways
30:47 What to do next

Sources:
- Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2025 (63% would cover a $400 expense with cash or its equivalent)
- Bankrate, Emergency Savings Report 2026 (share of Americans with no emergency savings or less than three months)
- Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, overdraft and NSF fee research (overdraft fees typically around $35)
- Edmunds, new vehicle financing data (average new car payment above $700 a month)
- IRS, filing season statistics (average federal refund around $3,000 in recent years)
- Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, Wage Growth Tracker (job switchers vs job stayers)
- Locke and Latham, goal-setting research (specific goals with deadlines improve results)

Photos: Wikimedia Commons contributors. Full credits and licenses: https://github.com/ryan-rover-money-channel/ryan-rover-money/blob/main/agendamento/creditos/video06.md

This video is for education only and is not financial advice. Numbers are illustrations, not promises.
